## Reproduced shipped boundary

- Official `pm-context@2026.10.10`, npm gitHead `49f1594f51e99f7306ccb7c9858287aa31765644`; downloaded tarball matches registry SHA-1 and SHA-512
- Installed `@unbrained/pm-cli@2026.10.11`, Node `v24.19.0`, Linux
- Public `buildContextPack`, `renderMarkdown`, `renderAgentHandoff`, and real installed `pm context-pack --include-deps` reproduce the association/implementation cases
- Current main `22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d` still has the same dependency projection statically. Its newer receipt work is source-only and was not executed in this review

## Observed versus expected

With one stored edge from item `a` to item `b`:

| Stored kind | Actual a.dependsOn | Expected a.dependsOn | Actual a.dependedBy | Expected a.dependedBy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| related | b | empty | empty | empty |
| implements | b | empty | empty | empty |
| blocked_by | b | b | empty | empty |
| blocks | b | empty | empty | b |

The positive `blocked_by` control passes. Both non-ordering controls and the inverse-ordering `blocks` control fail their intended assertions. All four raw `relationships[].kind` values remain correct. Markdown and agent renderers label the derived list literally as `a: depends_on [b]`, so it asserts ordering rather than merely showing all links.

The host's [dependency-kind contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/261a2e8f9ca235c42465bf26b8df2cbbc98d2228/docs/DEPENDENCY_KIND_CONTRACT.md) distinguishes association from ordering and defines `A --blocks--> B` as B waiting for A. The typed relationship registry is authoritative, including extension-defined semantics.

## Minimal public-SDK reproduction

In a new empty directory with `pm-context@2026.10.10` and `@unbrained/pm-cli@2026.10.11` installed from npm, run this ESM script. No tracker, provider, or model is needed:

```js
import { buildContextPack, renderAgentHandoff } from 'pm-context';

for (const kind of ['related', 'implements', 'blocked_by', 'blocks']) {
  const pack = buildContextPack([
    { id: 'a', title: 'Focus', type: 'Task', status: 'open',
      dependencies: [{ id: 'b', kind }] },
    { id: 'b', title: 'Context', type: 'Task', status: 'open' }
  ], { ids: ['a'], includeDeps: true,
       generatedAt: '2026-10-11T00:00:00.000Z' });
  console.log(kind, JSON.stringify(pack.relationships), JSON.stringify(pack.deps));
  console.log(renderAgentHandoff(pack));
}
```

Every case currently emits `a.dependsOn = ['b']`. The `related`/`implements` cases should retain their relationship and useful context without becoming scheduling dependencies. `blocks` must preserve the inverse scheduling direction.

A real CLI review also reproduces this on a copied four-item synthetic tracker: a venue-selection task has `related` forecast evidence and an `implements` governing decision. `pm context-pack --id bf-work --include-body --include-deps --format json` retains those types in `relationships`, but reports both IDs in `deps[].dependsOn`. Agent output claims `bf-work: depends_on [bf-proof, bf-rule]`. There are no ordering edges in that fixture.

## Cause and current source

`buildContextPack` iterates every extracted relationship and inserts `rel.to` into `dependsOn[rel.from]` without consulting kind, ordering semantics, or inverse direction. Both renderers then print `depends_on`.

- [Current projection, index.ts lines 573–592](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d/index.ts#L573-L592)
- [Markdown label, line 701](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d/index.ts#L695-L704)
- [Agent label, line 884](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d/index.ts#L878-L887)

## Impact and limits

An agent consuming the optional dependency summary can infer a prerequisite that is only evidence/association, or reverse who waits for whom. JSON still contains the accurate typed relationship list, and tracker files are not rewritten. This is a derived-output semantic defect, not demonstrated data loss, a provider defect, or a security vulnerability. Default full JSON without `--include-deps` completed the reviewed knowledge task correctly.

## Existing owners and duplicate check

All-status GitHub issue/PR searches for `depends_on`, `relationship`, `related dependsOn`, and non-blocking terms found no exact defect report. All 74 canonical tracker items at the pinned main revision were indexed. Adjacent owners:

- [PR 18: original include-deps addition](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/pull/18)
- [pm-context-qbmf: neighborhood traversal](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d/.agents/pm/features/pm-context-qbmf.toon)
- [pm-context-opzn: agent handoff rendering](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d/.agents/pm/features/pm-context-opzn.toon)
- [pm-context-ci6v: usage receipts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/22cc215d4a4f29525951e5b3c02c84c259a6918d/.agents/pm/features/pm-context-ci6v.toon), which does not address this projection

## Suggested acceptance

1. Build ordering summaries from the public relationship semantics, preserving direction for `blocked_by`/`blocks` and declared extension kinds
2. Retain non-ordering relationships and context with their correct kinds; do not drop them merely to fix the ordering summary
3. Cover association-only, implementation-only, direct ordering, inverse ordering, and mixed cases through public builder plus real CLI JSON/Markdown/agent output
4. Preserve source item/history bytes and existing raw typed relationships
5. If the intended surface is all relationships rather than ordering, make the schema and rendered labels explicit about that instead of calling them `dependsOn`/`depends_on`

No implementation changes are included in this report.
Dependency projection relabels non-ordering relationships as depends_on and reverses blocks

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Reproduced the issue ESM script verbatim in a new empty npm project with pm-context@2026.10.10 and @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.10.11 (Node v24.19.0). All four kinds retain their raw relationship but produce a.dependsOn=[b], b.dependedBy=[a]. related and implements falsely imply scheduling; blocks reverses execution order; blocked_by passes as the positive control. Agent output literally reports a: depends_on [b]. Imported only issue 136 atomically after duplicate searches and two dry runs selecting exactly one issue using --since 2026-10-11T10:07:00Z. UX gaps: github import offers no issue-number or limit selector; bare pm install pm-github fails and requires npm:pm-github. No extension installation state will be committed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Plan: resolve registered relationship definitions and use the SDK ordering orientation primitive for derived dependency summaries. Keep association, implementation, unknown kinds, raw edges and neighborhood context unchanged. Add public builder and installed CLI JSON/Markdown/agent regressions using real scratch trackers, including extension-defined semantics and byte-preservation checks. Prove failure by reverting only the projection and rebuilding before running the new tests.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Implementation uses the public registry ordering flag and precedence contract, whose omitted precedence defaults to source_before_target. The SDK orientation helper exists internally but is not exported through the public package entry points, so no internal SDK imports were introduced. Pure builder callers may supply relationshipRegistry; both commands resolve the active workspace registry. Regression fixtures install copied dist and manifest files into real scratch trackers; discovery ignores symlink-only extension roots.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Additional SDK/CLI gaps encountered while building extension-kind regressions: the host create --dep argument validator rejects registered custom relationship kinds as outside its built-in enum, and ItemMetadata dependency kinds are typed as the built-in union. The regression therefore imports extension-owned metadata with the real public commitImportedItem writer and tests active custom semantics through actual installed CLI commands. Scratch item IDs use the tracker prefix returned by the SDK. These host gaps are outside issue 136 and will be reported without filing changes elsewhere.

Failures include association-only, implementation-only, inverse blocks, mixed edges, and active custom semantics through installed CLI output. The blocked_by and depends_on controls pass. Restored the fixed projection and rebuilt dist. Earlier fixed focused run passed all 15 tests; final linked and release gates follow.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: History restoration round: CI health on the earlier review-fix push failed both Node matrix jobs because this item's history chain and item hash did not verify under the then-pinned 2026.10.10 host (history_drift; upstream unbraind/pm-cli#1458) - a newer host had written the 12:41 tests_update entry with a context the older pinned host rejects. The earlier response was to re-anchor the stream: history records 21-26 were REPLACED with versions recomputed by the pinned 2026.10.10 host plus a history_repair marker, and the item document lost its per-test updated_by/updated_at fields. That violates the append-only contract, so this change restores the original records 21-26 and the matching item document byte-exactly from the last pre-re-anchor commit (SHA-256 identical on both files), drops the recomputed replacements and the repair marker entirely, and bumps the @unbrained/pm-cli devDependency pin to 2026.10.13 so CI's pinned host verifies the newer-host tests_update entry instead of history being rewritten. The only genuinely new content added by the re-anchor commit was its CI-failure note, whose substance is preserved in this comment. Verified under the bumped pinned host: history --verify ok (26 entries, item hash matches the last restored record) and health --strict-exit --require-merge-drivers exits 0 with history_drift ok.
